title: performance.mark() from a content-script isolated world lands in the page's User Timing buffer — no bridge needed; jsdom lacks the API so stub it in tests
trigger: Instrumenting content-script code with performance.mark/measure and wondering whether page.evaluate can read the entries, or writing jsdom tests that call performance.mark
principle: Chrome's performance timeline is per-document, shared across isolated worlds — marks emitted by a content script appear in performance.getEntriesByType('mark'|'measure') when read via page.evaluate on the main world (verified on real Chromium, e2e/extension-latency-marks.spec.ts). No postMessage relay needed. In jsdom, performance.mark/measure/clearMarks do not exist — Object.assign stubs onto the performance object, don't jest.spyOn (spyOn throws 'property does not exist').

cases.context: lookup-latency-marks ship: dev-only cell:lookup:*/cell:audio:* marks emitted in popupLifecycle/useDictionaryToolbar (isolated world) were read directly by streamFlixPage.evaluate → real durations 30–300ms. The console.debug '[perf] <name>: <ms>ms' summary emitted alongside the measure doubles as a Playwright page.on('console') fallback surface.
cases.bad: jest.spyOn(performance, 'mark') → TypeError: Property mark does not exist in the provided object
cases.good: Object.assign(performance, { mark: markMock, measure: measureMock, clearMarks: clearMarksMock })

applyFor: any dev-only latency instrumentation in content scripts
jsdom tests touching the User Timing API
e2e specs asserting on performance entries
